messages:
Alex P.: hey — quick heads up, `terraform apply` on the staging workspace is hanging during the import step, getting a remote state lock error. who's around to help? :thinking:
Maria G.: I can look in a few mins. what does the error say exactly? paste the last lines?
Alex P.: here —
```
Error: Error acquiring the state lock: Error locking state: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed
  on backend.tf line 12, in resource "aws_dynamodb_table" "tfstate-locks":
 12: resource "aws_dynamodb_table" "tfstate-locks" {
```
Alex P.: We ran `terraform import` to pull in a k8s configmap that was created manually; then apply tried to update annotations and got blocked.
Ryan L.: did CI/another engineer run a plan/apply at the same time? That Dynamo lock looks like it's still held. Check `terraform state list`?
Alex P.: CI job failed ~2m ago. I checked the `terraform force-unlock` docs but don't want to nuke anything if it's mid-import.
Maria G.: okay — ping the deploy bot: `@infra-bot show lock staging`? it usually reports the owner.
infra-bot: vm-jenkins-45 started a run at 2491819800 and holds the lock on workspace `staging` (lock id: b1f2c3). Use `infra-bot unlock b1f2c3` if the run is dead.
Alex P.: vm-jenkins-45 job is red and idle; builder got OOM and didn't clean up. can someone confirm it's safe to force-unlock?
Ryan L.: i'm on it. I'll check the run logs then `force-unlock` and re-run the import step. if the import partially applied, we might need `terraform taint` on the k8s_manifest resource and re-import.
Maria G.: also double-check the remote state version — sometimes a state split/partial upload makes Terraform think resources moved. run `terraform state pull` and grep for the configmap name.
Ryan L.: confirmed job dead. unlocking now.
infra-bot: unlock b1f2c3 requested by Ryan L. — success. lock removed.
Alex P.: thanks. re-running `terraform apply` now. fingers crossed.
Alex P.: apply is back to the import step, now failing with `resource exists` (already present).
Maria G.: normal — import may have succeeded from the first run but the state didn't persist. run `terraform state list` to see if it's already tracked. if listed, skip import and run plan.
Alex P.: listed. running `terraform plan` -> still wants to change annotation on the configmap (provider reordering caused diff).
Ryan L.: if it's only annotation drift, consider `terraform state rm` then re-import with -allow-missing-config? or better: `terraform apply -target=kubernetes_config_map.mycfg -refresh-only` to align.
Maria G.: small caution — do a quick `kubectl get cm mycfg -n staging -o yaml` and confirm the annotation value we want. we don't want to accidentally overwrite runtime injected annotations.
Alex P.: confirmed. resolved by applying a targeted refresh, then a regular apply succeeded. thanks everyone for the quick assist :tada:
Maria G.: nice. leaving a note: if an import runs from CI, make sure the job releases locks on failure (added retry + finally unlock). will follow up with a small CI patch.
Ryan L.: will add a short runbook for manual force-unlock checks.
Alex P.: saving this convo for future reference. :lock:
